images.title: Half line through two circles
images.purpose: Show 9/18 as exactly half of a circle cut into 18 equal pieces and 7/15 as a little less than half of a circle cut into 15 equal pieces, each with a half line, so the child sees 9/18 = 1/2 and 7/15 is less than 1/2.
images.composition: Two round circles side by side, each cut into equal pieces with shaded pieces counted from the top clockwise and a vertical half line through its centre, with its counts and its result written under it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two flat circles of the same size, each 300 px across (radius 150), thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), centres on one level at y 350 and at x 400 (left) and x 1056 (right). Cut lines are thin dark straight lines (2 px) from the centre to the edge, counted from 12 o'clock clockwise. LEFT CIRCLE: exactly 18 lines make exactly 18 equal pieces of 20 degrees each; the first 9 pieces from 12 o'clock clockwise (the right half of the circle, 12 to 6 o'clock) are filled teal #0072B2 and the other 9 pieces are white. RIGHT CIRCLE: exactly 15 lines make exactly 15 equal pieces of 24 degrees each; the first 7 pieces from 12 o'clock clockwise (12 o'clock to 168 degrees, which stops short of 6 o'clock) are filled amber #E69F00 and the other 8 pieces are white. Through the centre of each circle one straight vertical half line in reddish purple #CC79A7, 6 px thick, from 20 px above the top of the circle to 20 px below its bottom (it lies on cut lines in the left circle and runs through the middle of the 8th piece in the right circle). Above each half line the text half line (30 px, dark #1F2937, about y 150). At the top left of each circle the part letter (a) at x 210 and (b) at x 866 (44 px, bold, dark, about y 120). Under each circle, about y 560, its caption in dark (36 px): 9 of 18 pieces under the left circle and 7 of 15 pieces under the right circle. Under each caption, about y 660, its result in dark bold (64 px, the largest text in the frame): 9/18 = 1/2 under the left circle and 7/15 < 1/2 under the right circle. In all 33 pieces, of which 16 are shaded (9 teal, 7 amber). Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
the half line drawn anywhere except straight through the centre from top to bottom
a circle with a different number of pieces or shaded pieces than 18 with 9 and 15 with 7
images.takeaway: 9 of 18 pieces fill exactly one half, so 9/18 = 1/2, while 7 of 15 pieces stop short of the half line, so 7/15 is less than 1/2.
images.description: Two circles with a half line through each, one cut into 18 equal pieces with 9 shaded and one cut into 15 equal pieces with 7 shaded, with 9/18 = 1/2 and 7/15 < 1/2 written under them.
images.context: Concept image for Half as a Reference. It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (a paratha cut into equal pieces with half of the pieces shaded, a line marking the half) and shows the concept's own example, 9/18 and 7/15.
images.teaching_notes: Look at where the half line falls: it sits between pieces 9 and 10 on the left and in the middle of piece 8 on the right, so 7 pieces fall short. The slip to watch is that a fraction close to a half, like 7/15, is called equal to a half.

image_decisions.why: The half line through two circles cut into 18 and 15 equal pieces shows 9/18 on the half and 7/15 short of it.
